steps: Gather your brand, product and persona documents with your brand team, and tidy them into one agreed set, removing old or conflicting rules.
Upload or enter your brand, product and persona guidelines in GenStudio for Performance Marketing, with the channel guidelines, logos, colors and tone of voice.
Test generated output against each guideline with a set of sample briefs for ads and email, and adjust the guidelines where the output drifts.
Review the test results with your brand reviewers, record their sign-off, and publish the guidelines so editors and collaborators can begin their work.
deliverables: Published brand, product and persona guidelines
Tidied source documents and guideline inventory
Output test results and brand sign-off record
asks: Your current brand, product and persona documents, including logos, colors and tone of voice rules
A brand reviewer who can settle conflicting rules and sign off the test output
risk: Guidelines that conflict or leave gaps lead to off-brand drafts: we settle each conflict with your brand reviewer and test generated output before publishing.
outcome: Your editors and collaborators start work from published brand, product and persona guidelines that the generative AI uses as guardrails.

steps: Agree the template list with your marketing team, by channel and format for email, Meta and display, and collect the approved designs for each.
Design and code responsive HTML templates for each agreed format, and adapt each one with Handlebars content placeholders.
Upload each template to GenStudio for Performance Marketing and test it with sample content, checking the layout on phones and desktops.
Load the approved assets editors will use into Content, named to an agreed convention, and record each template and asset in a register.
deliverables: Responsive HTML templates for email, Meta and display
Approved assets loaded into Content
Template test results and template register
asks: Approved designs and brand rules for each channel format you want templates for
The final approved assets, such as logos, images and product shots, for editors to use
risk: A template that renders badly in one channel or on one screen size: we test each one with sample content before editors use it.
outcome: Your editors build campaign content for email, Meta and display from tested templates and approved assets held in Content.

steps: Agree with your media team which Meta, LinkedIn and Campaign Manager 360 ad accounts to connect, and who holds the ad account permissions for each.
Connect the ad account for each paid ad channel, signed in as a GenStudio system manager or editor with the right ad account permissions.
Check that historical data from your active campaigns, media and ads reaches Insights for each connected account.
Test activation of an approved ad experience into an existing campaign and ad set, and review it in inactive status in the channel's own ad manager.
deliverables: Connected Meta, LinkedIn and Campaign Manager 360 ad accounts
Insights data check for each account
Activation test results and permissions record
asks: An owner of each ad account who can grant the right permissions
An existing campaign and ad set in each channel that we can test activation into
risk: Missing ad account permissions stall activation: we list who holds each permission before connecting, and test one activation per channel before your team relies on it.
outcome: Approved ad experiences go from GenStudio for Performance Marketing to your connected channels for final review, and Insights receives your campaign data.

steps: Map your editors and approvers by role, and agree the first campaign to run end to end as the training project.
Train editors on prompting and creating experiences, using your own brand guidelines and templates, and show how guideline quality shapes generated content.
Walk editors and approvers through review and approval on the first campaign: editors request content review, approvers approve, and editors publish the approved drafts.
Activate the approved ad experiences with your team, review them in the channel's own ad manager, and record questions for a short follow-up session.
deliverables: Role-based training sessions and materials
First campaign run end to end
Quick-reference guide for editors and approvers
asks: The names and roles of the editors and approvers to train
A real first campaign, with its brief and approvers, to run during training
risk: Early drafts that miss the brand can put editors off: we run the first campaign alongside them and log any guideline gaps for your brand team.
outcome: Your editors and approvers have run a full campaign from prompt to activation, and can run the next one on their own.

steps: Review Insights each month by campaign, media and attribute, and agree with your team which ads are not performing well.
Create variations of those ads with the integrated generative AI, send them for review and approval, and refresh hero content where it has aged.
Update brand guidelines and templates as your brand changes, and report what changed and how the refreshed ads perform against the ones they replaced.
deliverables: Monthly Insights review and refresh report
Approved ad variations and refreshed hero content
Updated guidelines and templates
asks: An approver who can review and approve new variations each month
Notice of brand, product or campaign changes coming up in the month
risk: Calling an ad weak before its results settle: we agree a minimum run with your team first, and compare each variation with the ad it replaces.
outcome: Each month your weakest ads get approved variations, and your guidelines and templates stay current with the brand.

steps: Agree the branded domains for tracking links and landing pages with your IT team, and complete the initial setup steps and protocols for your Marketo Engage instance.
Set up SPF and DKIM, and the CNAMEs for branded tracking links and landing pages, with your IT team adding each record to your domains.
Install the Munchkin code on your website, and test visits on a sample of pages to confirm the people who visit are tracked.
Set up users and roles from an agreed access list, and record every setting, domain record and role in a setup log your team keeps.
deliverables: Configured Marketo Engage instance and admin settings
SPF, DKIM and CNAME records in place
Munchkin tracking on your website
Users, roles and setup log
asks: An IT contact who can add records to your sending and tracking domains
Access to your website code, or a web developer, to install the Munchkin code
The list of users and the roles each one needs
risk: Email without SPF and DKIM is more likely to be filtered as spam: we set up both before the first send and test them with your IT team.
outcome: Your Marketo Engage instance sends authenticated email from your own domains, with branded links and landing pages and visitor tracking in place.

steps: Agree the field mapping with your CRM admin before the first sync, field by field, in a mapping sheet that records owners and data types.
Connect Marketo Engage to Salesforce or Dynamics with your CRM admin, and choose which fields sync and which stay hidden.
Check that the sync is running correctly after the first sync, comparing a sample of records in both systems against the mapping sheet.
Record the final mapping, hidden fields and sync settings in a sync runbook, with who to call and what to check when records stop syncing.
deliverables: Agreed field mapping sheet
Marketo Engage connected to your CRM
Sync test results and sync runbook
asks: A CRM admin who can agree the mapping and set up the connection
A decision on which CRM fields marketing may see and which stay hidden
risk: A wrong mapping at the first sync puts bad values in many records at once: we agree every field with your CRM admin before it runs.
outcome: Marketo Engage and your CRM share the right data, with an agreed mapping, hidden fields kept hidden and a tested sync.

steps: Agree the program templates your team will clone, such as webinar, nurture, newsletter and event, and the naming rules each one follows.
Build each program template with My Tokens and its Smart Campaigns, each Smart Campaign with a Smart List and its flow steps.
Build the branded email templates, landing pages and forms in Design Studio from your brand rules, agreeing fields and consent wording with you.
Test each template by cloning it into a sample program, sending test emails, submitting test forms, and fixing issues before your team signs off.
deliverables: Program templates for webinar, nurture, newsletter and event
Branded email templates, landing pages and forms
Template guide with My Tokens list
Template test results and sign-off
asks: Your brand rules, approved designs and legal footer wording for emails and pages
A marketing lead who decides which kinds of programs become templates
risk: Teams changing cloned programs by hand drift from the standard: we build My Tokens into every template and give your team a guide to cloning each one.
outcome: Your team launches webinars, nurtures, newsletters and events by cloning tested program templates with branded emails, landing pages and forms.

steps: Run a data audit of your database, sampling records for gaps, duplicates and inconsistent values, and report what needs fixing first.
Build the program that standardizes incoming data, with Smart Campaigns that use Smart List filters and triggers to catch the records to fix, and test it on sample records.
Model lead scoring and the lead lifecycle in workshops with marketing and sales, agreeing the behaviors and attributes that score and the stages a lead passes through.
Build the scoring and lifecycle campaigns through to the MQL handoff, and test them on sample leads before the first leads reach sales.
deliverables: Data audit findings
Data standardization program
Lead scoring model and lifecycle map
Scoring and lifecycle campaigns, through to MQL handoff
asks: Marketing and sales leads who can agree scoring rules and the MQL definition
Access to your Marketo Engage database and the people who own its data
risk: Sales not trusting the leads passed at the MQL handoff: we agree scoring and the handoff with sales, and test against a sample of past leads first.
outcome: Your incoming data arrives standardized, leads are scored and moved through an agreed lifecycle, and sales receives leads at an MQL handoff it agreed.

steps: Map your marketing users by role, from email builders to campaign owners, and plan the sessions and exercises each group needs.
Train each group on programs, Smart Campaigns and templates, with hands-on exercises in your instance, from building a Smart List to setting a flow.
Document the new instance setup, from admin settings, CNAMEs and Munchkin to the data sync, templates and naming rules, so your team can run it.
Walk your instance owner through the documentation, answer open questions, and hand over the training materials for new starters.
deliverables: Role-based training sessions and materials
Instance setup documentation
Handover walkthrough with your instance owner
asks: The names and roles of the marketing users to train
An instance owner who takes over the setup documentation after launch
risk: Knowledge that stays with us after launch: we document every setting as we build and hand it to your instance owner in a walkthrough.
outcome: Your marketing users build programs and Smart Campaigns from your templates, and your team runs the instance from its own documentation.

steps: Review Admin, Marketing Activities, Design Studio and Database each month against a standing checklist for clean-up, deliverability and scoring changes.
Agree the fixes with your Marketo owner, in order of risk, and make the agreed changes, such as retiring unused assets or adjusting scores.
Report what we found, what changed and what is left, and keep a running log so each month starts from the last one.
deliverables: Monthly instance review report
Agreed fixes, made in your instance
Running change log
asks: A Marketo owner who agrees the fixes each month
Notice of new programs, campaigns or sales changes that affect scoring
risk: Small problems that build up between reviews, such as falling deliverability: we check the same areas every month and raise urgent issues straight away.
outcome: Your Marketo Engage instance stays clean and current, with deliverability and scoring reviewed monthly and every fix agreed with your Marketo owner.

steps: Add your admins and users in the Adobe Admin Console from an agreed access list, and claim each domain your tracked sites use.
List every tracked site, page template and form with your web team, and agree whether the script goes in hardcoded or through a tag manager.
Deploy the Marketo Measure JavaScript on every page and form of every tracked site, following the agreed method.
Test that sessions and form fills are captured on a sample of pages and forms from each site, and fix any gaps found.
deliverables: Admin Console users and claimed domains
Site and form inventory
Marketo Measure JavaScript on every tracked site
Tracking test results
asks: An Admin Console administrator who can add users and claim domains
A web or tag manager contact who can deploy the script on every site
The list of every site and form you want tracked
risk: Pages or forms missed by the script leave gaps in touchpoint data: we inventory every site and form first and test a sample from each.
outcome: Marketo Measure captures sessions and form fills across every tracked site, so touchpoint data comes from complete session data.

steps: Agree the route with your CRM admin: the standard installation with the Salesforce Package or Microsoft Dynamics Managed Solution, or the packageless route.
Install the Marketo Measure package in your sandbox first, test it, then install it in production, or set up the packageless route with a dedicated connected user.
Connect the CRM to Marketo Measure, and set the permission sets and page layouts for the users who need to see its data.
Check the connection on sample records with your CRM admin, and record the route, connected user, permission sets and page layouts in a runbook.
deliverables: Marketo Measure connected to your CRM in production
Permission sets and page layouts
Sandbox test results and setup runbook
asks: A CRM admin who can install packages in sandbox and production
A decision on the route, and a dedicated connected user for the packageless route
risk: An install that disturbs your live CRM: we install in your sandbox first, test with your CRM admin, and only then move to production.
outcome: Marketo Measure is connected to your Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics CRM, with the right users seeing its data through agreed permissions and layouts.

steps: Agree your UTM conventions with your marketing and media teams, and record every value in use in a channel mapping sheet.
Write the online channel rules from the agreed conventions, and the offline channel mapping to your CRM campaign types.
Set the campaign sync rules that turn campaign members into touchpoints, for the campaign types your team agrees should count.
Check on a sample of recent touchpoints that each lands in the right channel and subchannel, and fix the rules where one does not.
deliverables: Agreed UTM conventions and channel mapping sheet
Online channel rules and offline channel mapping
Campaign sync rules
Touchpoint check results
asks: Marketing and media leads who can agree the UTM conventions
Your list of CRM campaign types and what each one is used for
risk: Inconsistent UTM values put touchpoints in the wrong channel: we agree the conventions first, map every value in use, and check a sample after setup.
outcome: Your online and offline touchpoints land in the right channel and subchannel, following UTM conventions your teams agreed.

steps: List your ad accounts and the channels without a connection, and agree with your media team who holds the right roles on each account.
Connect each ad account to Marketo Measure with the right roles, so its spend is pulled in automatically, and set up tagging on ad URLs.
Switch on CRM campaign costs where your team uses them, and load spend for channels with no connection from figures your team supplies.
Reconcile spend in Marketo Measure against your own records for an agreed month, by channel, and fix any gaps before ROI reporting starts.
deliverables: Connected ad accounts with automatic spend
Tagging on ad URLs
Spend loaded for channels with no connection
Spend reconciliation by channel
asks: An owner for each ad account who can grant the right roles
Spend figures for the channels that have no connection, by month
risk: Missing or partial spend skews return figures: we reconcile spend against your own records by channel before anyone reads the ROI reporting.
outcome: Spend for every channel reaches Marketo Measure, pulled automatically from connected ad accounts or loaded for the rest, ready for ROI reporting.

steps: Map your lead, contact and opportunity stages with marketing and sales operations, and agree the order a record moves through your funnel.
Order the stages in Stage Mapping as agreed, and check sample records to see that their progression through the funnel reads correctly.
Walk your teams through the attribution models, from single-touch to multi-touch, and for the custom attribution model, where you use it, agree its stages and weights.
Review the touchpoint and segment settings with marketing and sales operations, record each decision, and recheck sample records after any change.
deliverables: Agreed stage order in Stage Mapping
Custom attribution model stages and weights, where used
Touchpoint and segment settings record
asks: Marketing and sales operations leads who can agree stage order and weights
Your current lead, contact and opportunity stage definitions from the CRM
risk: Stages in the wrong order make Marketo Measure misread your funnel: we agree the order with both teams and check sample records after mapping.
outcome: Marketo Measure reads your funnel in the right order, and your attribution models and settings reflect what marketing and sales agreed.

steps: Agree the questions each group needs the Discover dashboards to answer, from marketing to sales and leadership.
Walk your teams through the Discover dashboards and the ROI Dashboard on your own data, by channel, subchannel and campaign.
Agree the filters and segments each group reads, and record them in a short dashboard guide for each team.
Set the short list of revenue, pipeline and return views that leadership sees each month, and walk leadership through the first set.
deliverables: Dashboard walkthroughs for each team
Agreed filters and segments by group
Monthly leadership views for revenue, pipeline and return
Dashboard guide for each team
asks: Time from each group, and the questions each wants the dashboards to answer
A leadership sponsor who approves the short list of monthly views
risk: Each team reading different numbers for the same question: we agree one set of filters and segments per group and document them in the guide.
outcome: Marketing, sales and leadership each read the Discover dashboards with agreed filters, and leadership sees the same short list every month.

steps: Agree with your analytics lead which analysts need access, and how the data warehouse reader account is shared and stored safely.
Give your analysts access to the read-only data warehouse reader account, and test a connection from each analyst's tool.
Connect Adobe's Power BI or Tableau report template to the data warehouse, and adapt it to your channels and date ranges.
Reconcile the report's figures against the ROI Dashboard for an agreed period, and walk your analysts through the adapted report.
deliverables: Analyst access to the data warehouse reader account
Adapted Power BI or Tableau report
Reconciliation results and analyst walkthrough
asks: The analysts who need access, and who owns the shared account
Your channel names and the date ranges your reports use
risk: Figures in the BI report that differ from Marketo Measure: we reconcile them against the ROI Dashboard for an agreed period before analysts rely on them.
outcome: Your analysts read Marketo Measure data in your own Power BI or Tableau, through a shared read-only account and an adapted report.

steps: Enable touchpoints for new CRM campaigns each month, and load new spend so each channel's spend data stays current in Marketo Measure.
Review channel mapping against new UTM values and domains, and update the rules so new touchpoints land in the right channel.
Report attributed pipeline and revenue by channel to your marketing and sales leads, noting what changed in the month and why.
deliverables: Touchpoints enabled for new CRM campaigns
Updated spend and channel mapping
Monthly attributed pipeline and revenue report
asks: Notice of new CRM campaigns, domains and UTM values each month
New spend figures each month for the channels we load ourselves
risk: New campaigns, UTM values or domains that nobody sets up leave touchpoints missing or in the wrong channel: we review each one every month before reporting.
outcome: Each month your attributed pipeline and revenue report by channel reflects new campaigns, new spend and new UTM values and domains.

steps: Agree with your marketing and analytics leads who needs access and what each group may do, from people who build models to people who read plans.
Create the Permissions role with the Marketing Campaign Analytics resource and its harmonized data, model and plan permissions.
Add the sandboxes and the dataset and schema permissions to the role, and assign the agreed users.
Have one user from each group sign in and test access, and record the role, sandboxes and users in an access register.
deliverables: Permissions role with Marketing Campaign Analytics permissions
Sandboxes, dataset and schema permissions
Assigned users and access register
asks: The list of users and what each one needs to do
An Experience Platform administrator who can create roles and assign users
risk: A missing permission stops Marketing Campaign Analytics working for a user: we test access with one user from each group before anyone starts work.
outcome: Your users reach Marketing Campaign Analytics in the right sandboxes, with the permissions their work needs and no more.

steps: Inventory your marketing data with your data team: channel spend and effort, conversions, and internal and external factors, with each source's owner and level of detail.
Model schemas on the XDM ExperienceEvent or Summary Metrics classes for your event level and aggregate data, with date and granularity on every aggregate schema.
Ingest each source with consistent dates, granularity and channel fields, agreeing one channel list with your teams so every dataset names channels the same way.
Validate the loads against your source totals by channel and period, and record each dataset, its schema and its refresh in a data register.
deliverables: Schemas on XDM ExperienceEvent or Summary Metrics classes
Ingested spend, effort, conversion and factor datasets
Load validation results
Data inventory and register
asks: A data team contact for each source, with access to its files or system
Your channel list, and the history of spend and conversions to load
Agreement on which internal and external factors to include
risk: Sources that name channels or dates differently cannot be compared: we agree one channel list and date rules first, and validate each load against source totals.
outcome: Your spend, effort, conversions and factors are ingested for Marketing Campaign Analytics with consistent dates, granularity and channels, checked against your own totals.

steps: Define the harmonized fields with your analytics lead, and record in a mapping sheet which field in each dataset feeds each one.
Write the dataset rules for each aggregate, event and factor dataset, mapping their fields to the harmonized fields, with conflict resolution rules where datasets overlap.
Define your marketing touchpoints and conversions with your marketing and analytics leads, in agreed definitions each team signs off.
Sync the harmonized data and check it against the source datasets by channel and period, fixing rules until every difference is explained.
deliverables: Harmonized fields and mapping sheet
Dataset rules for every dataset
Agreed touchpoint and conversion definitions
Harmonized data check results
asks: An analytics lead who can agree the harmonized fields and settle conflicts
Marketing sign-off on what counts as a touchpoint and a conversion
risk: Overlapping datasets that count the same activity twice: we write conflict resolution rules where they overlap and check harmonized totals against each source.
outcome: Your marketing datasets are merged into harmonized data, with touchpoints and conversions defined the way your teams agreed, ready for modeling.

steps: Agree the outcome to model with your marketing and finance leads, with the conversion, the touchpoints, the lookback and training windows, and the factors to include.
Configure the models with those settings and the priors your teams agree, and turn on multi-touch attribution where agreed.
Train the models and review the fit with your analysts, checking that results make sense against what your teams know about each channel.
Retrain and rescore as findings emerge, adjusting settings and priors until the fit suits the business, and record each run and change.
deliverables: Configured and trained models
Model settings and decision record
Fit review with your analysts
asks: Marketing and finance leads who agree the outcome to model and the priors
Analysts' time to review each training run against what they know
risk: A model that fits the data but not the business: we review each run with your analysts and retrain until the results hold up against what they know.
outcome: You have trained models that measure the outcome you specify across your channels, with settings and priors your teams agreed.

steps: Agree the first budget plans with your marketing and finance leads: the budget, business units, channels, flight dates and channel constraints.
Build the plans in Marketing Campaign Analytics, one per scenario, allocating budget by business unit and channel from the trained models' outcomes.
Compare the impact of each plan scenario with your leads before they decide, and record the plan they choose and why.
Train marketing and finance users to read model and plan insights, with exercises on your own plans and a short guide.
deliverables: First budget plans by business unit and channel
Scenario comparison and decision record
Training sessions and guide for marketing and finance
asks: Your budget, flight dates and any channel constraints for the plans
Marketing and finance users to train, and time for the sessions
risk: Plans that finance does not trust go unused: we build the first plans with marketing and finance together and train both to read the insights.
outcome: Your marketing and finance teams compare budget plans by business unit and channel, and read model and plan insights on their own.

steps: Load the month's new spend, conversion and factor data, and check it against your source totals before rescoring.
Rescore the models manually once the new data is added, and retrain them where findings or business changes call for it.
Rebuild the plans on the rescored models, and report ROI and budget shifts to your stakeholders with the reasons behind each change.
deliverables: Monthly data loads, checked against source totals
Rescored or retrained models
Rebuilt plans and monthly ROI report
asks: The month's spend, conversion and factor data from each source owner
Notice of business changes, such as product launches or promotions, that affect the models
risk: Plans built on models that missed the latest data: we rescore after every monthly load and rebuild the plans before reporting to stakeholders.
outcome: Each month your models and plans reflect the latest spend, conversions and factors, and your stakeholders see ROI and budget shifts.

steps: Agree the user types with your marketing operations lead, from administrators to all-access users and read-only users, and who belongs to each.
Set up the product profile and a user group for each user type in the Admin Console, and add the agreed users.
Create the administrator, all-access and read-only roles in Experience Platform Permissions with the Marketo Optimizer sandbox and product permissions, and add each group to its role.
Test access with one user of each type, and record the groups, roles and permissions in an access register your team keeps.
deliverables: Product profile and user groups in the Admin Console
Administrator, all-access and read-only roles
Access test results and access register
asks: The list of users and the user type each one needs
An Admin Console administrator who can create user groups and add users
risk: Users given more access than their work needs: we agree each user type first and test every role before your team starts building.
outcome: Each person on your team reaches Marketo Optimizer through the right user group and role, with the permissions their work needs.

steps: Agree the sending subdomain and the delegation method, fully delegated or CNAME, with your IT team, and delegate the subdomain to Adobe.
Set the DMARC policy with your IT team, check SPF and DKIM on the sending subdomain, and review the IP pool.
Create an email channel configuration for each brand, region and message type, binding its subdomain, IP pool and sender identity.
Have your IT team allowlist the sending addresses, then send test emails from each configuration to your own inboxes and record the results.
deliverables: Delegated sending subdomain
DMARC policy, with SPF and DKIM checked
Email channel configurations by brand, region and message type
Allowlisted sending addresses and test results
asks: An IT contact who can change your domain records and set the DMARC policy
Your brands, regions and message types, and the sender identity for each
risk: Email from a new subdomain that fails authentication or is blocked internally: we check SPF, DKIM and DMARC and have IT allowlist the addresses before the first send.
outcome: Your email sends from a delegated subdomain, with authentication in place and a channel configuration for each brand, region and message type.

steps: Agree in a workshop the program types your marketing team needs, with the attributes, status steps and success statuses for each.
Define each agreed program type in Marketo Optimizer, and set up the folder and program structure with naming rules your team signs off.
Create the My Tokens that folders and programs inherit, and test them in a sample program before your team builds real programs.
Record the program types, folders and tokens in a short guide, so your team knows which type and folder each new program uses.
deliverables: Program types with attributes and statuses
Folder and program structure
Inherited My Tokens
Program structure guide
asks: Marketing leads who can agree the program types and success statuses
Your current naming rules and the kinds of programs you run
risk: Program types defined too loosely make results hard to compare: we agree each type's status steps and success statuses in the workshop before building any programs.
outcome: Your programs follow agreed types, folders and inherited My Tokens, so each new program starts from the right structure.

steps: Agree with your marketing team the audiences your journeys need, and decide for each whether it is a dynamic or a static people list.
Build the dynamic and static people lists with filters on activity, company and person attributes, using the derived persona and person engagement score as filters.
Review with your marketing team how your leads behave, and set the engagement score weighting model that fits them.
Check each list's membership against sample people your team knows, and record each list's purpose and rules in an audience register.
deliverables: Dynamic and static people lists
Engagement score weighting model
List membership checks and audience register
asks: A marketing lead who can agree the audiences and the scoring weights
Examples of known leads and accounts to check list membership against
risk: Lists that catch the wrong people put them in the wrong journeys: we check membership against known people before any list feeds a journey.
outcome: Your journeys draw on tested people lists, with personas and an engagement score weighted to how your leads behave.

steps: Agree the first person journeys with your marketing team in a design workshop, mapping each one's audience, steps, messages and goal in a journey map.
Build each journey inside its program: the audience entry by dynamic list or by event, and the wait, split and listen-for-event steps.
Add the email actions and data changes, set the start and end dates and the re-entry settings, and record each choice in the journey map.
Check each journey with test leads on every path before it goes live, then publish it and watch the first entries with your team.
deliverables: Published first person journeys
Journey maps with every setting recorded
Pre-launch journey test results
asks: A marketing lead who agrees each journey's audience, messages and goal
Approved email content for each journey's email actions
risk: A journey that sends the wrong message or reaches the same person too often: we test every path and the re-entry settings with test leads before publishing.
outcome: Your first person journeys are live inside their programs, each tested on every path and documented in a journey map.

steps: Agree the email templates and reusable parts with your brand team, and which headers, logos and legal content authors must not change.
Build the email templates and reusable visual fragments in the design space, and use content locking to protect the agreed headers, logos and legal content.
Set up personalization with fallback text for every personalized field, and test it with sample records that lack those values.
Write the first emails from the templates with your team, have your reviewers check each one, and publish them.
deliverables: Email templates with locked brand and legal content
Reusable visual fragments
Personalization with fallback text, tested
First published emails
asks: Your brand rules, approved legal text and footer content for emails
Reviewers who check and sign off the first emails
risk: Authors editing legal or brand content by mistake: we lock those parts in every template, so authors change only the sections meant for them.
outcome: Your authors build emails from locked templates and reusable fragments, with personalization that falls back to agreed text when data is missing.

steps: Add next best path steps to the agreed journeys, writing a prompt for each path that describes your intent in natural language.
Run simulations on a sample audience, review the path chosen for each person and its reasoning with your team, and tune the prompts.
Turn on journey traffic control for overlapping journeys, setting the importance of each scoring dimension and writing the journey descriptions the model reads.
Run a simulation before the weights go live, agree the results with your team, and record the prompts, weights and decisions in a decision log.
deliverables: Next best path steps with tested prompts
Journey traffic control weights and journey descriptions
Simulation results and decision log
asks: A marketing lead who agrees the scoring weights for journeys whose audiences overlap
Time from your team to review simulation results and the AI's reasoning
risk: AI path choices your team cannot explain: we review each simulated decision and its reasoning with you, and you can review or override any recommendation before activation.
outcome: Your journeys choose each person's path from prompts your team tested, and journey traffic control gives priority to the best journey when audiences overlap.

steps: Agree the landing page subdomain with your IT team, and set up the subdomain and the landing page presets.
Create the form presets, each with its streaming connection and dataset in Experience Platform, so marketers can create and publish forms.
Agree your standard forms with marketing and legal, field by field with consent wording, then build them and the landing pages that carry them.
Publish the forms and landing pages, submit test entries on each, and check the data arrives in the dataset.
deliverables: Landing page subdomain and presets
Form presets with streaming connection and dataset
Published standard forms and landing pages
Form submission test results
asks: An IT contact who can set up the landing page subdomain
Agreed form fields and consent wording from marketing and legal
risk: Form data that never reaches Experience Platform: we test each published form end to end and check every submission arrives in its dataset.
outcome: Your marketers publish forms and landing pages from ready presets, and every submission lands in its Experience Platform dataset.

steps: Agree the opt-in, opt-out and help keywords and their replies with your marketing and legal teams, and the first messages to send.
Connect your WhatsApp Business Account with its API credentials, set up the webhooks with the agreed keywords and replies, and configure the WhatsApp channel.
Build the first WhatsApp messages from templates Meta has approved, and add them to the agreed person journeys.
Test opt-in, opt-out and help replies and each message on test phones before journeys go live, and record the setup in a channel runbook.
deliverables: Connected WhatsApp Business Account and channel configuration
Opt-in, opt-out and help keywords and replies
First WhatsApp messages in journeys
Test results and channel runbook
asks: Access to your WhatsApp Business Account and its API credentials
Message templates Meta has approved for the first messages
Legal sign-off on the opt-in, opt-out and help replies
risk: Messages reaching people who have not opted in or have opted out: we test opt-in and opt-out handling on test phones before any journey with WhatsApp messages goes live.
outcome: Your person journeys can send WhatsApp messages from approved templates, with opt-in, opt-out and help replies tested and working.

steps: Agree with your marketing team how often a person may be contacted, by channel and communication type, and at what hours.
Build the channel rule sets with the agreed frequency caps and quiet hours, and activate them.
Apply the rule sets to the email actions in your journeys, and check with test leads that caps and quiet hours hold.
deliverables: Agreed contact frequency and quiet hours policy
Active channel rule sets
Rule sets applied to journey email actions
asks: A decision on contact limits and quiet hours from marketing and legal
risk: Caps set too tight can hold back important messages: we agree which communication types each cap covers and check the rules with test leads before journeys go live.
outcome: People receive your email within frequency caps set by channel and communication type, and outside the agreed quiet hours.

steps: Agree with your marketing team the email actions where timing matters, and the personas or segments that need different content in one email.
Turn on send-time optimization for those email actions, with the delivery window and the wait step it requires.
Build conditional content rules so one email shows a different block to each persona or segment, agreeing the wording of each block with your team.
Test each conditional block with test leads from every persona or segment, and record which actions use send-time optimization and why.
deliverables: Send-time optimization on agreed email actions
Conditional content rules by persona or segment
Test results and settings record
asks: Content for each persona or segment's block, approved by your team
A marketing lead who agrees where send timing matters
risk: The wrong block shown to a persona or segment: we test every block with test leads from each group before the email goes live.
outcome: Selected journey emails go out at the time each profile is predicted most likely to engage, and one email shows each persona or segment its own block.

steps: Map your marketers by role, from email authors to journey builders, and plan the sessions each group needs.
Train every group on the Home page, where they start AI conversations, launch skills and open marketing workspaces, and on programs and people lists.
Train journey builders and email authors on the marketing workspace, journeys and email authoring, with exercises built on your own programs.
Hand over a short guide to your naming rules and a checklist for publishing, and walk your team lead through both.
deliverables: Role-based training sessions
Naming rules guide
Publishing checklist
Handover walkthrough with your team lead
asks: The names and roles of the marketers to train
Your naming rules, or a lead who can agree them
risk: Marketers publishing journeys or emails without the agreed checks: we train on your own programs and hand over a publishing checklist each team follows.
outcome: Your marketers work in Marketo Optimizer on their own, from the Home page to published journeys and emails, following your naming rules.

steps: Review journey results, email performance, list membership and traffic control decisions each month, using the Coworker chat interface to explore journey metrics.
Agree the changes with your marketing lead, then tune audiences, path prompts and score weights, recording each change and its reason.
Report the month's findings and next steps to your team, comparing results before and after each change made the previous month.
deliverables: Monthly journey and audience review report
Tuned audiences, path prompts and score weights
Change log with reasons
asks: A marketing lead who agrees the changes each month
Notice of new campaigns, products or audiences that affect journeys
risk: Too many changes at once hide what worked: we agree a short list of changes each month and compare results against the month before.
outcome: Each month your journeys, audiences, path prompts and score weights are reviewed and tuned, with findings and next steps reported to your team.

steps: Create the Marketo Qualifier and Marketo Qualifier Admins user groups in your Admin Console, with the names and product profile Adobe specifies.
Add the optional group for managers who read email performance reports, then add your users, with every administrator also in Marketo Qualifier Admins.
Agree the opt-out footer wording with your legal team, and set it in the global email opt-out settings so it goes on every outbound email.
deliverables: Marketo Qualifier and Marketo Qualifier Admins user groups
Users added, with the optional managers' group
Opt-out footer on every outbound email
asks: The list of representatives, administrators and managers who need access
Approved opt-out footer wording from your legal team
risk: An administrator outside Marketo Qualifier Admins cannot configure CRM connections, the Knowledge Center or opt-out settings: we add every administrator to it and check access first.
outcome: Your representatives, administrators and managers reach Marketo Qualifier through the right user groups, and every outbound email carries your opt-out footer.

steps: Work with your CRM administrator to set up the connected app or app registration, with the read-only access the first connection needs.
Enter the Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365 connection in Marketo Qualifier, and agree whether to grant the write access that activity synchronization and opt-out write-back need.
Map the prospect, contact, account and opportunity fields representatives see in the inbound mapping, marking the ones they filter and target by.
Check imported records against your CRM for a sample of accounts and prospects, and record the mapping and access in a connection runbook.
deliverables: Connected app or app registration with agreed access
Marketo Qualifier connected to your CRM
Inbound field mapping, with filter and targeting fields marked
Import check results and connection runbook
asks: A CRM administrator who can set up the connected app and grant access
A decision on whether to allow write access for activity sync and opt-out write-back
Sales leaders who agree the fields representatives see and target by
risk: Representatives seeing too many fields, or missing the ones they target by: we agree the mapping with sales leaders and check it on sample records.
outcome: Marketo Qualifier imports the CRM fields your representatives need, shown where they expect and marked for filtering and targeting.

steps: Arrange the one-time Microsoft 365 administrator approval with your IT team where your policy requires it, before representatives connect.
Connect each representative's Outlook mailbox and calendar with them, and set their signature, meeting length, buffers, working hours and booking link.
Write the email drafting context with your sales leaders, setting your tone and structure, and check that a test booking lands on the right calendar.
deliverables: Connected Outlook mailboxes and calendars
Booking links and meeting settings for each representative
Email drafting context for your tone and structure
asks: An IT contact who can give the Microsoft 365 administrator approval if required
Each representative's working hours, meeting length and buffer preferences
risk: Representatives who do not finish connecting cannot send or take bookings: we connect each one in a short session and track progress against your team list.
outcome: Marketo Qualifier drafts in your tone and structure, sends from each representative's mailbox, recognizes replies and schedules meetings on their calendar.

steps: Gather your sales playbooks, ideal customer profiles, positioning guides and collateral with your sales and marketing leads, keeping only current, approved versions.
Set the company name and URL, and upload the documents in PDF, PPTX or DOCX format to the Knowledge Center.
Build the playbook with your sales leaders, agreeing the plays, profiles and positioning it holds.
Test that drafted emails and chat answers use your messaging on a set of sample prospects, and adjust the documents where they drift.
deliverables: Curated set of current sales documents
Knowledge Center playbook
Messaging test results on sample prospects
asks: Your current sales playbooks, ideal customer profiles, positioning guides and collateral
A sales leader who approves the playbook and reviews test drafts
risk: Old or conflicting documents lead to off-message drafts: we keep only current, approved versions and test drafts on sample prospects before representatives use them.
outcome: Drafted emails and chat answers draw on your current sales materials in the Knowledge Center, in your own messaging.

steps: Agree the first Outbound Workflows with your sales leaders, each with its goal and the targeting filters that pick its prospects.
Build each workflow's cadence of email, phone and LinkedIn steps from the AI's proposal, with touchpoint prompts, send window, time zone and sharing.
Review the first generated emails and the AI's reasoning with your representatives, and adjust prompts and targeting before anyone is enrolled.
Enroll the first prospects with your sales leaders once they sign off, with each email approved by the prospect's owner before it is sent.
deliverables: First Outbound Workflows, built and shared
Reviewed first emails and agreed prompts
Sign-off record from your sales leaders
asks: Sales leaders who set each workflow's goal and targeting
Representatives' time to review the first generated emails and reasoning
risk: Generated emails that miss your message or target the wrong prospects: we review the first emails and the AI's reasoning with representatives before anyone is enrolled.
outcome: Your representatives run their first Outbound Workflows, with cadences and emails reviewed by your team and every email approved before it is sent.

steps: Prepare each prospect list that is not in your CRM as a CSV file, cleaning duplicates and adding the CRM lead ID where there is one.
Import each CSV file, mapping the standard fields and any custom or additional columns so generated emails can use them.
Check a sample of imported prospects against the source file, and review a generated email that uses a custom field.
deliverables: Cleaned CSV files for each prospect list
Imported prospects with custom fields mapped
Import check results
asks: The prospect lists to import, with where each one came from
Confirmation that each list may be used for outreach
risk: Duplicate prospects in a list getting extra outreach: we clean each file of duplicates before import and check a sample of imported prospects against the source file.
outcome: Prospects from outside your CRM are in Marketo Qualifier with their custom fields mapped, ready for generated emails to use.
